source.body:
### Bug Description

`saveToMemory` in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/memoryManagement.ts` takes `previousStepsCount` and does `steps.slice(previousStepsCount)` "to avoid duplicates (they're already in memory)". Both call sites in `nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/runAgent.ts` pass `response?.metadata?.previousRequests?.length`.

But `previousRequests` is the accumulator of the earlier tool rounds of the SAME execution: `buildResponseMetadata` → `buildSteps` pushes `previousRequests` back into `steps` on every engine round-trip. Memory is written exactly once, at the end of the turn. Nothing from those earlier rounds was ever saved, so the slice drops every round except the last one.

Effects on the next turn: the model cannot see the tools it already called (in our workflow it repeats a 16k-char `read_instructions` tool call every turn), it loses data fetched in earlier rounds (we traced a confabulated "I already cancelled those" to this), and because the replayed history differs from what the live turn sent, prompt caching of the history across turns is impossible.

The code is unchanged on master (2.45.0). The slice was introduced in #23687. Related: #14361 (V1/V2 save no tool calls at all) and #29148 (proposes gating V3 tool-step persistence on `returnIntermediateSteps`). Whichever persistence policy is chosen, the slice as written dedups against nothing.

Proposed fix: pass all `steps` of the execution to `saveToMemory` (or drop the `previousStepsCount` parameter). We run that one-line change as a patch on the compiled file; with it the replayed history equals the live turn and the repeated tool calls stop.

### To Reproduce

1. Chat Trigger → AI Agent (typeVersion 3.x) with an Anthropic or OpenAI chat model, Simple Memory, and three tools.
2. Send a message that makes the agent call tool A, then (in a second round) tools B and C, then answer.
3. Inspect the Simple Memory node's `saveContext` output in the execution, or send a follow-up and look at the `loadMemoryVariables` output.
4. The stored history is: HumanMessage, AIMessage(tool_calls: B, C), ToolMessage(B), ToolMessage(C), AIMessage(final). Round A is missing.
5. Ask "which tools did you use?" — the model answers B and C only, and will call A again if it needs its result.

### Expected behavior

The full sequence of the turn is stored: HumanMessage, AIMessage(tool_calls: A), ToolMessage(A), AIMessage(tool_calls: B, C), ToolMessage(B), ToolMessage(C), AIMessage(final). `buildSteps` already assembles exactly that list; only the slice in `saveToMemory` removes it.

comments.author: Raizesdaterra
comments.text:
We hit the same root cause with a more severe effect on Anthropic models that enforce preserved-thinking prefix binding (Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, on accounts created on or after 2026-08-31).

Setup: n8n 2.43.5 self-hosted, AI Agent V3, Anthropic Chat Model claude-haiku-5-5 (Thinking Mode not set, so the model thinks), Simple Memory, one HTTP Request Tool.

In one turn the agent called the same tool twice (two sequential rounds). Simple Memory stored only the second round: HumanMessage, AIMessage [thinking, tool_use], ToolMessage (second result), AIMessage (final text). The signed thinking block in the stored AIMessage was created after the first round, so on the next user message Anthropic rejects the replay:

400 messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. [...] Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.0.content.0`.

Every following message in that session fails the same way, so the conversation gets stuck, not just loses context. Saving all tool rounds (#41577) should resolve this, as long as each round is replayed exactly as it was sent (see also #40360: tool inputs replayed as input: {} when thinking is on, which would still change the prefix).
